questions.prompt: Your phone is lost or stolen. Which call protects your money first?

options.text: Your bank's 24×7 helpline, to freeze UPI, net banking, and cards
A friend, just to share what happened
options.explanationWrong: A friend cannot freeze your bank accounts or UPI IDs. Call your bank first.

options.text: The number inside an SMS claiming 'we found your phone'
options.explanationWrong: Scammers send fake 'found phone' texts to extract PINs or login codes.

options.text: Nobody until the next morning
options.explanationWrong: Waiting gives a thief time to abuse your SIM and OTPs.

questions.explanationCorrect: Banks have 24×7 emergency helplines. Freezing UPI and cards stops financial drainage first.

questions.prompt: Why should you contact your mobile operator right after freezing your bank accounts?

options.text: To block the lost SIM card so thieves cannot receive your bank OTPs
To claim a free replacement phone
options.explanationWrong: Telcos block your SIM/number to stop SMS OTP hijacking; they don't give free phones.

options.text: To erase your bank statements
To change your UPI PIN through SMS
options.explanationWrong: Blocking the SIM stops anyone from using your mobile number.

questions.explanationCorrect: Even if a lost phone is locked, a thief could move an unlocked SIM into another phone to intercept OTPs unless you block the SIM.

questions.prompt: After freezing your bank and SIM, why must you sign out and change passwords on your email and cloud accounts?

options.text: Saved passwords, password-reset emails, and backup photos live in those accounts
Because blocking a SIM automatically locks your email too
options.explanationWrong: Email and cloud sessions stay logged in over Wi-Fi even after a SIM block.

options.text: Only to free up cloud storage space
options.explanationWrong: This is about locking out active sessions on the stolen phone.

options.text: So your old phone rings louder
options.explanationWrong: Changing passwords & signing out cuts off remote access on the lost device.

questions.explanationCorrect: Email and cloud accounts can still run on Wi-Fi on a lost phone and hold password resets and documents—change passwords and sign out everywhere.

questions.prompt: An SMS arrives on your spare phone: 'Your lost device was located—log in with your screen lock & bank PIN to claim it.' What do you do?

options.text: Ignore the link—never enter PINs or passcodes on unsolicited recovery links
Enter only your screen passcode so they can unlock the phone
options.explanationWrong: Giving away your screen lock hands a thief full access to your banking apps.

options.text: Reply with your last 4 card digits
options.explanationWrong: Never send card or identity details to unknown numbers.

options.text: Call the random mobile number back immediately
options.explanationWrong: Calling scam numbers exposes you to social engineering.

questions.explanationCorrect: Thieves often send fake 'device found' phishing links to steal screen passcodes or cloud passwords. Never tap them.

questions.prompt: Which official number and portal handle cyber fraud & device misuse reports in India?

options.text: Helpline 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in (plus CEIR to block the lost IMEI)
Any phone repair shop in the neighbourhood
options.explanationWrong: Local shops cannot block bank accounts or log police cybercrime tickets.

options.text: A sponsored search ad promising instant phone tracking
options.explanationWrong: Ads can be fake phishing traps—type official government portals directly.

options.text: Social media direct messages
options.explanationWrong: Social media DMs are not official reporting routes.

questions.explanationCorrect: Report financial risk or fraud on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in, and file a lost-phone police/CEIR report to block the handset IMEI.

questions.prompt: What is the safest order of actions when you realise your phone is missing?

options.text: 1. Freeze bank & UPI → 2. Block SIM → 3. Secure email/cloud passwords → 4. Report officially
1. Post on social media → 2. Wait a day → 3. Call your bank
options.explanationWrong: Every minute of delay increases OTP and app risk; freeze bank and SIM immediately.

options.text: 1. Buy a new phone case → 2. Ignore SIM block → 3. Change wallpaper
options.explanationWrong: Immediate financial and SIM lockdown is critical.

options.text: 1. Call the thief's 'found phone' link → 2. Share passcode
options.explanationWrong: Never share passcodes or reply to suspicious recovery texts.

questions.explanationCorrect: Bank first, SIM second, account sign-outs third, then official reporting stops both money theft and identity takeover.
